title: Cold rebuild: A quantum-readiness inventory
summary: Rebuild A quantum-readiness inventory from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **A quantum-readiness inventory** in *Quantum computers and post-quantum crypto*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Grover's search halves the effective bits of a symmetric key. What does this print?
steps.explain: AES-256 keeps 128-bit security even against a quantum attacker, which is why long-lived data should use 256-bit keys.

steps.title: Rebuild A quantum-readiness inventory cold
prompt: Write a program that reads algorithm names from standard input, one per line until the end (skip blank lines), and prints a verdict for each, then a summary:
- `AES-256`, `SHA-256`, `SHA-384`, `SHA-512`, `HMAC-SHA256`, or names starting with `ML-KEM`, `ML-DSA` or `SLH-DSA`: `<name>: ok`
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
